item.text:
**1B.3 Research Note: Ali Khamenei in 2024**

**Bottom line:** I did **not** find strong evidence that Khamenei materially strengthened nuclear command-and-control discipline, custody, safety, or accident-prevention safeguards in 2024. The record is mixed: there were some restraint signals and late-year talks about capping stockpiles and adding inspectors, but the dominant 2024 evidence is the opposite direction - inspector restrictions, unresolved safeguards problems, and brinkmanship language from figures close to him.

**Accepted claims**

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `Iran offers concessions to prevent censure resolution at IAEA meeting` | Reuters / Iran International | 2024-11-19 | [link](https://www.iranintl.com/en/202411196621) | Reuters reported that Iran offered to cap its near-weapons-grade uranium stockpile at about 185 kg and to consider admitting four additional experienced IAEA inspectors. This is the clearest 2024 evidence of a possible step toward tighter custody and verification, though it was conditional and not a demonstrated reform by Khamenei personally. | `1B.3` |
| `IAEA Board passes resolution against Iran on cooperation, inspectors` | Reuters | 2024-06-05 | [link](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/iaea-board-passes-resolution-against-iran-on-cooperation-inspectors-3472087) | Reuters said the IAEA Board called on Iran to reverse its barring of inspectors and to cooperate fully, after Iran had barred many of the agency’s top enrichment experts. That is strong evidence against strengthened safeguards in 2024 and suggests deteriorating discipline and verification. | `1B.3` |
| `Iran says nuclear weapons have no place in its nuclear doctrine` | Reuters | 2024-04-22 | [link](https://www.yahoo.com/news/iran-says-nuclear-weapons-no-085328983.html) | Iran’s foreign ministry reiterated that nuclear weapons were not part of its doctrine, and Reuters noted that Khamenei has final authority over nuclear policy and had previously banned nuclear weapons in a fatwa. This supports a restraint-oriented public line, but it is declaratory rather than proof of better command-and-control or safety safeguards. | `1B.3`, `1B.2` |
| `Iranian commander warns Tehran could review 'nuclear doctrine' amid Israeli threats` | Reuters | 2024-04-18 | [link](https://www.yahoo.com/news/iranian-commander-warns-tehran-could-114201991.html) | A senior IRGC commander in charge of nuclear security said Israeli threats could push Tehran to review and deviate from its nuclear doctrine. That is evidence of brinkmanship in Khamenei’s orbit, not of disciplined accident-prevention or custody safeguards. | `1B.3`, `1B.2` |

**Assessment**

- The **best positive evidence** is the November Reuters report on a possible stockpile cap and additional inspectors.
- The **best negative evidence** is the June IAEA resolution and inspector-barring issue, which points to weaker verification and less robust safety discipline.
- I found **no solid 2024 primary-source evidence** that Khamenei personally announced or implemented a meaningful new command-and-control or nuclear safety reform package.

**Search gap**
- I did not find a credible 2024 source showing Khamenei ordering specific accident-prevention measures, tighter chain-of-command procedures, hardened custody rules, or a formal nuclear safety overhaul.
- What exists is mostly indirect: official nonproliferation rhetoric, inspection diplomacy, and conflict-driven brinkmanship. That is enough to support a mixed or weak negative reading, but not a strong affirmative one.
